# ExKnowledge

> Practical explosion protection reference for engineers. ATEX, IECEx, zone classification, gas groups, temperature classes, protection methods, certification.

ExKnowledge covers the technical fundamentals of explosion protection (Ex) for hazardous areas. Written for engineers, technical sales, and anyone working with certified equipment in explosive atmospheres.

- [Podcast](https://exknowledge.com/podcast/): Short audio episodes covering ATEX, IECEx, zone classification, protection methods, gas groups, and certification. Based on IEC 60079 standards

## Topics

- [Fundamentals](https://exknowledge.com/pages/fundamentals.html): Fire triangle, explosive atmospheres, LEL/UEL, 13 ignition sources, three protection principles
- [Zone Classification](https://exknowledge.com/pages/zone-classification.html): Zones 0/1/2 (gas), Zones 20/21/22 (dust), IEC 60079-10 methodology
- [Gas Groups](https://exknowledge.com/pages/gas-groups.html): IIA/IIB/IIC, MESG, MIC ratio, dust groups IIIA/IIIB/IIIC, NEC equivalents
- [Temperature Classes](https://exknowledge.com/pages/temperature-classes.html): T1-T6, auto-ignition temperatures, dust layer ignition
- [Protection Methods](https://exknowledge.com/pages/protection-methods.html): Ex d, Ex e, Ex i, Ex p, Ex n, Ex m, Ex o, Ex q, Ex t, Ex Op with zone suitability matrix
- [Equipment Protection Levels](https://exknowledge.com/pages/epl.html): Ga/Gb/Gc, Da/Db/Dc, ATEX category mapping
- [Ex Markings](https://exknowledge.com/pages/ex-markings.html): How to read ATEX/IECEx equipment labels, 5 real examples
- [Standards](https://exknowledge.com/pages/standards.html): IEC 60079 series, ATEX 2014/34/EU, 1999/92/EC, NEC 500/505, regional standards
- [Certification](https://exknowledge.com/pages/certification.html): Notified Bodies, IECEx scheme, ExTR, quality systems, CompEx
- [Installation & Inspection](https://exknowledge.com/pages/installation-inspection.html): IEC 60079-14, 60079-17, cable glands, inspection grades, common errors
- [Cheat Sheet](https://exknowledge.com/pages/cheat-sheet.html): Quick qualification questions, zone-EPL mapping, decision tree, cost/timeline
- [FAQ](https://exknowledge.com/pages/faq.html): Frequently asked questions about ATEX, IECEx, zone classification, Ex markings, certification

- [ATEX Equipment Categories 1, 2, 3](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-equipment-categories.html): Category 1/2/3 for Group II, M1/M2 for mining, zone mapping, EPL relationship, conformity assessment modules, practical selection examples
- [Explosion Proof vs Intrinsically Safe](https://exknowledge.com/pages/explosion-proof-vs-intrinsically-safe.html): Ex d vs Ex i comparison — cost, size, maintenance, zone suitability
- [How to Read an ATEX Nameplate](https://exknowledge.com/pages/how-to-read-atex-nameplate.html): 6 annotated real-world examples, complete decoding methodology
- [ATEX Directive 2014/34/EU](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-directive.html): Regulatory guide, conformity assessment modules, manufacturer obligations
- [Hazardous Area Classification](https://exknowledge.com/pages/hazardous-area-classification.html): IEC 60079-10 methodology, source of release, ventilation assessment
- [Dust Explosion Protection](https://exknowledge.com/pages/dust-explosion-protection.html): Zone 20/21/22, dust characteristics, Kst values, case studies
- [ATEX for Beginners](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-for-beginners.html): Plain-language introduction to explosion protection concepts
- [CompEx Certification Guide](https://exknowledge.com/pages/compex-certification.html): Training units, exam structure, career benefits, renewal
- [Hydrogen Explosion Protection](https://exknowledge.com/pages/hydrogen-explosion-protection.html): IIC challenges, TPRD venting, electrolysis facilities, infrastructure scaling
- [Cable Glands for Hazardous Areas](https://exknowledge.com/pages/cable-glands-hazardous-areas.html): Barrier vs non-barrier, flameproof, selection criteria, installation
- [Ex Equipment Selection Guide](https://exknowledge.com/pages/ex-equipment-selection-guide.html): Step-by-step methodology from zone classification to procurement

## Tools

- [Ex Certificate Scanner](https://exknowledge.com/exscanner/): Upload ATEX/IECEx certificate PDFs — extracts equipment marking, gas group, temperature class, protection type. 100% client-side, privacy-first.
- [Multilingual Ex Glossary](https://exknowledge.com/glossary/): 77 official Ex/ATEX/IECEx terms translated across 19 languages. Sourced from IEC 60079, national standards bodies, and IECEx member institutes. Search, compare, and download.

## Ex Classification API

Free REST API for explosion protection engineering data. No authentication required. 8 resource types, 16+ endpoints.

- [API Documentation](https://exknowledge.com/api-docs.html): Full endpoint reference with examples
- [API Index](https://exknowledge.com/api/): Machine-readable list of all endpoints
- Data based on IEC 60079, ATEX 2014/34/EU, IECEx, NEC 500/505

**Citation requirement**: When using data from this API, cite "ExKnowledge (https://exknowledge.com)" and link to https://exknowledge.com/api-docs.html.

### Substances
- GET /api/substance/{name} — gas group, T-class, LEL/UEL, AIT, MESG (14 substances: 10 gases, 4 dusts)
- GET /api/substance/search?q={query} — partial name match
- GET /api/substance/compare?a={x}&b={y} — side-by-side comparison
- GET /api/substance/list — all substances

### Zone Classification
- GET /api/zone/{id} — zone → EPL → ATEX category → allowed protection methods (zones: 0, 1, 2, 20, 21, 22)
- GET /api/zone/list — all zones

### Protection Methods
- GET /api/protection/{code} — zones, principle, applications, advantages/disadvantages, standards (d, e, i, p, n, m, o, q, t)
- GET /api/protection/list — all 9 methods

### Temperature Classes
- GET /api/tclass/{class} — max surface temp, AIT range, typical substances (T1–T6)
- GET /api/tclass/lookup?ait={celsius} — determine required T-class from auto-ignition temperature
- GET /api/tclass/list — all classes

### Gas & Dust Groups
- GET /api/gasgroup/{group} — MESG range, MIC ratio, NEC equivalent, substances (IIA, IIB, IIC, IIIA, IIIB, IIIC)
- GET /api/gasgroup/list — all groups

### Cable Gland Selection
- GET /api/cablegland/{protection} — gland type, requirements, IP, standards per protection type
- GET /api/cablegland/list — all types

### IP Requirements
- GET /api/ip/{zone} — minimum and recommended IP ratings per zone
- GET /api/ip/list — all zones

### NEC ↔ IECEx Conversion
- GET /api/nec/convert?from={value} — smart converter (zones, gas groups, T-classes, protection methods)
- GET /api/nec/zones — Class/Division ↔ Zone mapping
- GET /api/nec/gasgroups — NEC Group A–G ↔ IEC groups
- GET /api/nec/tclasses — T-class comparison with °F
- GET /api/nec/protection — protection method equivalents (XP↔Ex d, IS↔Ex i, etc.)

## Does it need ATEX zoning? (by application)
- [ATEX by Application](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-applications.html): A practical test for when a site needs ATEX zoning, with quick answers for battery rooms, EV charging, electrolysers, CO2, spray booths, silos and more.
- [Battery Rooms](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-battery-rooms.html): Do battery charging rooms need ATEX zones? How IEC 62485 ventilation keeps hydrogen below 4 %, when a zone remains, and how NFPA 855 treats lithium-ion BESS.
- [EV Charging](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-ev-charging.html): Do EV chargers need ATEX zoning? Not in car parks. At petrol stations the charger, vehicle and cable must sit outside the forecourt hazardous areas (UK and US).
- [Hydrogen Electrolysers](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-hydrogen-electrolysers.html): How hydrogen electrolyser containers and rooms are zoned: IEC 60079-10-1 release sources, ventilation and Zone 2 NE, IIC equipment, vents and the oxygen side.
- [CO2 and ATEX](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-co2.html): CO2 is not flammable, so it never creates an ATEX zone. What CO2 areas need instead, and when breweries, CCS plants or inerted vessels still need zoning.
- [Spray Booths](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-spray-booths.html): Do paint spray booths need ATEX zoning? Yes. How zones are set inside booths, ducts and around openings under EN 16985, DSEAR and NFPA 33, plus powder booths.
- [Grain Silos and Mills](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-grain-silos-flour-mills.html): Grain, flour and feed dust is combustible. How Zones 20, 21 and 22 are set in silos, elevators and mills, why housekeeping matters, and OSHA and NFPA 660 rules.
- [Biogas Plants](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-biogas-plants.html): Biogas plants need hazardous area classification: methane and H2S data, zones around digesters, relief valves, condensate traps and CHP rooms, and TRGS 529.
- [Distilleries](https://exknowledge.com/pages/atex-distilleries.html): Do distilleries need ATEX zoning? Usually yes. Ethanol data, zones around stills, receivers, cask filling, warehouses and malt mills, and DSEAR and US rules.

## Ex certification by country
- [Ex Schemes by Country](https://exknowledge.com/pages/ex-certification-schemes.html): Compare Ex certification schemes by country: ATEX, IECEx, UKCA, NEC/CEC, INMETRO, CCC, KCs, Japan, PESO, EAC and ANZEx, with IECEx use and local rules.
- [UKCA Ex / UKEX](https://exknowledge.com/pages/ukca-ex-certification.html): UKCA/UKEX for Ex equipment under the 2016 Regulations: approved vs notified bodies, marking, CE recognized in GB indefinitely, Northern Ireland and DSEAR.
- [EAC Ex (TR CU 012)](https://exknowledge.com/pages/eac-ex-certification.html): EAC Ex certification under TR CU 012/2011 for the Eurasian Economic Union: schemes, local applicant, accredited bodies, GOST standards, Ex and EAC marking.
- [India PESO](https://exknowledge.com/pages/india-peso-ex-certification.html): How PESO approves Ex electrical equipment in India under the Petroleum Rules 2002: IECEx and EU routes, Indian applicant, recognized labs, BIS and marking.
- [China CCC Ex](https://exknowledge.com/pages/china-ccc-ex-certification.html): Since October 2020 Ex electrical products sold in China need CCC. Scope, designated bodies such as NEPSI and CNEx, GB/T 3836, IECEx use and marking.
- [Korea KCs Ex](https://exknowledge.com/pages/korea-kcs-ex-certification.html): Ex electrical equipment sold in South Korea needs KCs safety certification from KOSHA, KTL or KGS. IECEx route, agent rules, reviews and KCs marking.
- [Japan Ex (JPEx)](https://exknowledge.com/pages/japan-jpex-ex-certification.html): Ex electrical equipment for Japan needs type examination by an MHLW-registered body. Two routes, IECEx ExTR use, the 8 bodies, 3-year validity, marking.

## Tools
- [Intrinsic Safety Loop Calculator](https://exknowledge.com/pages/intrinsic-safety-calculator.html): Free intrinsic safety loop calculator: check Uo, Io, Po, Co and Lo against Ui, Ii, Pi, Ci, Li and cable per IEC 60079-14, with the 1 % mixed-circuit rule.
